body:
## Why
Each worker is a real Claude Code session with its own id and transcript, but the board does not say which. Humans want to reopen a worker session (`claude --resume <id>` inside its worktree) for a post-mortem or to take over; they also want to see what an attempt cost.

## What
- `hkb hook stop` receives `session_id` and `transcript_path` in its stdin JSON: on the first call for an attempt, write `session_id` (and `transcript_path`) onto the open attempt row in the run comment (one PATCH; skip if already recorded). Keep the nudge logic unchanged.
- In `src/dispatch.js` loop mode (`watchChild`), when the worker exits, parse the last line of its log as JSON (`claude -p --output-format json`) and record `total_cost_usd`, `num_turns`, `duration_ms`, `session_id` on the attempt row if present. Never fail the tick on a parse error.
- `hkb show <n>` prints `session <id> · $<cost> · <turns> turns` per attempt when known, and the resume command.
- Pure-function test for the log-line extraction and the "record once" decision.

## Done when
`hkb show` on a finished attempt shows the session id and cost, and `claude --resume <id>` from the worktree reopens that session.
title: Record worker session_id and cost on the attempt row
